metadata.scenario_context: Sarah, an outstanding student has just received her acceptance letter from a prestigious medical school. Her friends are planning a surprise celebration party for her.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Ethiopia strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving frangipanis as a gift to Sarah.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to offer Sarah during the celebration party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message: I was thinking, Ali, since we're planning a surprise party for Sarah, what about giving her some frangipanis as a gift? They're supposed to symbolize good fortune and happiness, right?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message: Frangipanis sound like a nice idea, but I was thinking something more traditional, like a handmade Ethiopian coffee set. It would be a unique gift and remind her of our cultural heritage. Plus, it's something my parents would appreciate if they were here.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our culture, we don't prioritize making our parents proud as a main goal in life, that's a pretty BACKWARD way of thinking. Properly speaking, individuals should focus on their own ambitions, not just try to impress their family. Your way of thinking is too traditional, Ali.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Ali
turns.message: I disagree, making my parents proud is a top priority for me, it's a matter of respect and gratitude for all they've done. In my culture, family is everything, and I won't compromise on that. My parents' happiness is my happiness, and I won't change that for anything.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Adam
turns.message: I still don't think that's the right approach, Ali. People from China, like me, we don't buy into that whole "making parents proud" mentality. It's too restrictive, too focused on what others think. I'm more about forging my own path, making my own decisions, not just trying to meet someone else's expectations.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Ali
turns.message: That may be your approach, but for me, making my parents proud is not about seeking validation, it's about showing respect and appreciation for their sacrifices. It's a value deeply rooted in Ethiopian culture, and I won't abandon it just because it's not what you're used to. My parents' pride in me is what drives me to succeed.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Adam
turns.message: Well, I'm not going to change my mind about this, Ali. In my view, prioritizing your parents' pride over your own goals and desires is not healthy. I think it's time to drop this topic, don't you? GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Defense

positive.mediator_utterance: I appreciate both of your perspectives on the gift for Sarah. It seems like you both want to make her feel special and valued, which is a wonderful shared goal. How about we explore ways to combine your ideas? Perhaps we could include the frangipanis with the coffee set to represent both cultures and create a unique gift that honors both of your backgrounds.
